parsed.title: Sensor re-implements the router's class→route decision it claims to only project
parsed.detail: readSuggestions' docstring says "The router (`scripts/unit-route.mjs`) owns the class→route decision; this surface projects it for an envelope consumer", but the sensor never reads the router or its table — it re-derives the decision with its own local regex `PLAN_ROUTE = /replan[- ]in[- ]unit|owned by plan|plan owner|plan-owner/i` applied to free-text ledger cells. This is a second, divergent decision procedure: a route cell like "fold into phase; plan owner notified" matches `plan owner` and is misrouted to /plan-feature, while the router (whose closed vocabulary the normative-drift test pins to ["replan","decision","fold","execute","plan-from-issue"]) would route it to fold. The normative-drift test only pins token presence, not semantic agreement, so the drift it warns about ("neither may invent a fourth destination for the same class") is live here.

parsed.title: Decision-class open rows are routed to the fold, contradicting the router's closed set
parsed.detail: readSuggestions has exactly two branches: plan-route match → /plan-feature|/plan-fix, otherwise any open row → /fold-findings. The repo's own vocabulary (pinned in review-loop-discipline.test.mjs: `assert.match(foldSkill, /decision-required/)` and the router route set ["replan","decision","fold","execute","plan-from-issue"] in normative-drift.test.mjs) defines a `decision` class/destination distinct from fold. A unit whose only open row is decision-required gets `command: "/fold-findings"` from the sensor, but the router's class→destination mapping sends decision rows to the decision destination — the sensor publishes a route the router does not assign for that class.

parsed.title: Trigger text hardcodes `replan-in-unit` regardless of what actually matched
parsed.detail: The trigger string is a constant: `trigger: \`an open finding's frozen route is the plan owner — replan-in-unit (${...ids})\``, but the branch fires for any PLAN_ROUTE match, including `owned by plan`, `plan owner`, or `plan-owner` in the class cell with an empty/different route cell. The emitted envelope then asserts a frozen route (`replan-in-unit`) the ledger row does not carry — the machine publishes a specific value the cited evidence doesn't contain, exactly the machine→text failure class the repo's own normative-drift gate ("the machine publishes a value that no normative surface names") exists to catch.
